## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:changes`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:changes` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Correct, fail-closed HOST-write guard with strong process-level tests; detector contract and emit format verified against existing hooks; documented text-parsing limits are non-blocking by design.
findings:
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:78-84 (writes_to_github / MINTS_BOT_TOKEN) — MINTS_BOT_TOKEN.search() matches `gh-app-token.sh` anywhere in the command and allows the ENTIRE command, so a compound line mixing an unauthenticated write with a token-mint elsewhere (e.g. `echo gh-app-token.sh && gh issue create`) is allowed. Explicitly scoped out by the docstring as a text-based honest-path guard; non-blocking, but worth noting as a false-negative surface.
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:64 (GIT_PUSH regex) — GIT_PUSH does not match forms like `git -C /path push` because a bare non-flag/non-assignment arg between `git` and `push` breaks the alternation. Common `git push origin main` is caught and tested; this edge form is an accidental-path false negative consistent with the control's stated limits.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Security (code changed)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Strong, well-tested fail-closed gate, but the bot-token whitelist matches "gh-app-token.sh" anywhere in the command, letting a benign host `gh` write bypass the deny — the exact incident class it targets.
findings:
- high scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:65 (MINTS_BOT_TOKEN) / :95-101 (writes_to_github) — The whitelist uses MINTS_BOT_TOKEN.search(command) over the whole command string, so any command containing the literal 'gh-app-token.sh' — even in an issue/PR body or an unrelated echo — is treated as 'minting the bot token' and ALLOWED. On a HOST session `gh issue comment 1816 --body "see gh-app-token.sh"` or `echo gh-app-token.sh; gh pr merge 1816` bypasses the deny and writes under the founder's account, which is precisely the accidental/honest-path incident class the gate exists to prevent…
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:132-142 (deny message) — The deny reason always suggests the remedy `GH_TOKEN="$(~/.claude/scripts/gh-app-token.sh)" gh …` even when the blocked verb is `git push`. Minting GH_TOKEN does not re-route git push authentication (git uses the credential helper/SSH), so the suggested remedy is misleading for the push case. Recommendation: tailor the remedy text to the matched verb, or drop the `gh …` example when denying git push.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Architecturally sound: a well-scoped, reversible dev-time PreToolUse gate that fits the existing hook pattern, honors invariant 2 (fail-closed) and invariant 3 (repo-local blast radius), with a correct hook contract and honestly-stated limits.
findings:
- low docs/decisions/ (absent) — Non-blocking (reversible in <1 day, so no DR is mandatory). This introduces a new enforcement gate that converts session-identity.sh's report into a refusal and cites incidents tied to DR-050; the DR traceability convention (issue->DR->artifact) would benefit from either a short DR recording the fail-closed enforcement decision or an explicit note in the hook/#1816 that no DR was minted by design. Consider linking Triggered by: #1816 in a DR or noting the deliberate omission.
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:38 — The gate depends on an out-of-repo, host-installed detector at ~/.claude/scripts/identity-boundary-check.sh (--location) that is not version-controlled here, so the gate's behavior is defined by an external contract. This is handled safely (absence => fail-closed deny) and mirrors session-identity.sh's existing coupling, but the cross-boundary dependency on an unversioned script's exit-code contract (0=container, 1=host, else=unknown) is worth documenting as a contract so a future change to tha…
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Every claim is backed by verifiable proof — docstring citations resolve to real file:line, and process-level tests genuinely exercise each named invariant; no unproven superlatives or false status signposts.
findings:
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:44 (docstring) — The comment 'measured 14-16ms over five runs' is an unverifiable performance assertion with no artifact in the diff. Non-blocking: it justifies a live-call-per-invocation design choice rather than making a correctness/status claim, and the surrounding rationale (fail-closed, limits) is otherwise well-cited and honest.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:blocked`

> ⏳ **The AI reviewer could not run — this is NOT a review of your code.**
>
> Almost always the **Claude subscription session quota** is exhausted (also possible: rate-limit / overload). The required `ai-review` check is `action_required` — it blocks merge only because un-reviewed code must not land — and it **re-runs automatically** when the quota window resets (the `ai-review-retry` workflow).
>
> **Options:**
> 1. **Wait** for the quota window to reset — the retry workflow re-reviews automatically.
> 2. **Fail over to PAYG API** — set repo variable `AI_REVIEW_FAILOVER=payg` + secret `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; re-runs then use pay-as-you-go instead of the subscription quota.
> 3. Re-run the `ai-review` workflow manually once quota is back.

<details><summary>reviewer output (redacted — may include the reset time)</summary>

```
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_BEGIN
reason: quota
evidence: NONE (reason is inferred, not observed)
classified_via: stdout(strict)
stderr_bytes: 0
stdout_bytes: 25
detail: |
  (no diagnostic text on either stream — see #1630)
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_END
```
</details>

_Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]`. Transient/quota failures are surfaced as `ai-review:blocked` (distinct from `ai-review:changes`) so a token outage never masquerades as a code-review verdict._

## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:pass`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:pass` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Correct, well-tested fail-closed PreToolUse gate blocking credentialed GitHub writes from HOST sessions; all six-ish invariants preserved, docstring claims verified, only documented in-scope limitations remain.
findings:
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:56 (GH_COMMAND) / writes_to_github — GH_COMMAND is anchored at segment start, so a segment led by a grouping/subshell token that is not in SEGMENT_SPLIT — e.g. `{ gh pr merge 1; }` or `(gh pr merge 1)` — begins with `{`/`(` and fails the anchor, so the gh write is ALLOWED on the host. Same for `command gh ...`. The docstring explicitly scopes the control to accidental/honest paths and disclaims deliberate circumvention, so this is within stated limits and non-blocking; noting because leading `(` subshells are moderately common in …
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:120 (location) + .claude/settings.json Bash matcher — Operational consequence worth flagging: the gate fails closed on 'unknown', so in any real container where ~/.claude/scripts/identity-boundary-check.sh is NOT installed (as in this very CI environment per the SessionStart banner), every `gh` write and `git push` from the Claude Bash tool is DENIED. This is the intended invariant-2 behavior, not a bug, but it makes installing the detector in the agent container a hard prerequisite for legitimate agent writes; ensure the container provisioning sh…
- info scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:139 GIT_PUSH (non-anchored) — GIT_PUSH.search is not anchored, so a segment merely containing the literal text `git push` inside a string (e.g. `echo "run git push"`) is denied on the host. Over-blocking is the safe direction and unlikely in practice; no action required.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Security (code changed)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: New host-write-guard PreToolUse hook correctly denies ambient-credential GitHub writes from HOST/unknown sessions, fails closed per invariant 2, no injection/secrets/deps; only non-blocking hardening notes remain.
findings:
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:79 (GH_TOKEN_SET regex) — The GH_TOKEN= remedy is text-only and cannot confirm the value resolves to a non-founder identity. If the documented form `GH_TOKEN="$(broker.sh)"` is used and the broker fails to an empty string, gh may fall back to the ambient founder credential while the gate ALLOWS the call — the exact incident class, reachable via an honest broker failure. The docstring acknowledges the value isn't knowable from text, so this is an accepted limitation; at minimum, tighten GH_TOKEN_SET to require a non-empt…
- info scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py: writes_to_github / docstring — The gate denies ALL `gh` invocations on host (including read-only ones like `gh pr view`, per the pipeline test), but the deny message and function name (`writes_to_github`) frame it as refusing a 'write'. Safe over-approximation with an available remedy, but the naming/wording is slightly misleading; consider aligning the prose or naming.
- trivial scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:import shutil — `import shutil` is unused (location() uses os.path.isfile/os.access, not shutil.which). Dead import; remove it.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Architecturally sound, in-scope, repo-local security gate that fails closed correctly; only non-blocking consistency/traceability notes.
findings:
- low packages/minspec/tests/host-write-guard.test.ts:1 — Test-placement convention drift: existing tests for scripts/hooks/* are pytest/stdlib files co-located in scripts/hooks/ (test_spec_gate.py, test_canonical.py). This hook's tests are a vitest TS suite under packages/minspec/tests/, coupling the package test run to python3 availability and a repo-root file outside the package. Reasonable if intentional (CI coverage via npm test), but inconsistent with the established boundary — worth a one-line rationale or moving to a co-located pytest. Non-blo…
- low docs/decisions/INDEX.md — A new enforcing security-gate posture is introduced (the escalation of session-identity.sh from report to gate) and the code references DR-050 and the incident history, but no DR records this control or its relationship to DR-008 (dispatch security). Not blocking because the change is trivially reversible (<1 day), but a short DR would make the why traceable per DR-023/traceability convention. Non-blocking.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Claims are backed by real process-level tests and truthful sibling-file citations; gate fails closed per invariant 2, no unproven status/superlative claims.
findings:
- low scripts/hooks/host-write-guard.py:75 (GH_TOKEN_SET) — `GH_TOKEN=` with an empty value (`GH_TOKEN= gh ...`) is treated as an explicit identity and ALLOWED, yet gh would fall back to the ambient founder credential. Non-blocking: squarely within the docstring's stated scope (accidental/honest-path guard, explicitly not a forgery defense). Noted for the record only.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

commits.messageBody:
Root cause: `scripts/hooks/session-identity.sh` already DETECTS this exact
condition and prints a warning, but it is a report, not a gate - one exit
(`exit 0` at :34 and :103), invoked from `session-start.sh:25` as `... || true`
under a comment reading "Never fatal". It refuses nothing. Nothing else read its
verdict either: a repo-wide grep found it consumed only by its own unit test.
Meanwhile PreToolUse covered `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` and not `Bash`, so a host
session's `gh` and `git push` - which act as the FOUNDER by construction - passed
through ungated. #1816 measured the consequence twice: a comment accepting
DR-050's amendment posted under the founder's account, and a fabricated founder
decision that kept security issue #1482 closed for ten days.

This adds the missing refusal as a PreToolUse deny on `Bash`, the mechanism
spec-gate.py already uses. The rule is deliberately small: provably in the
container, allow and change nothing; anywhere else, deny a command that invokes
`gh` or `git push` unless it mints the bot token first - the remedy the existing
warning already tells the agent to use.

Fail-closed per constitution invariant 2: a detector that is missing, not
executable, times out, or exits unexpectedly DENIES and names which. Verified by
mutation - making either unknown-location arm return "container" reddens the
suite. Fail-closed applies to the WRITE, not to every command; denying all Bash
would make a host session unusable for the diagnosis that tells the human to
relaunch it.

Location is read LIVE (measured 14-16ms over five runs, two /proc reads), never
from session-identity.sh's 30-minute cache: a cached verdict attests to a past
measurement, never to the act being gated.

Alternatives rejected (DR-086 section 4, recorded because under autonomy=act
nobody sees them live):
- Making session-identity.sh exit non-zero. `session-start.sh` swallows it with
  `|| true`, and a SessionStart failure does not block a later tool call, so it
  would stay a report.
- Denying every Bash command on the host. Leaves no path to diagnose or to
  relaunch, and the threat is specifically credentialed writes.
- An env-var override to make the gate answerable in tests. An override that
  changes the verdict is a bypass; tests stub the detector via HOME instead.
- A denylist of `gh` write subcommands. That is the #2124 matcher-boundary shape:
  any enumeration of write verbs is incomplete the day a new one ships.

Stated limit, so it is not read as stronger than it is: this reads the command
TEXT, so a process intent on evading it can. It raises a one-command mistake to
deliberate circumvention, which is what both measured incidents actually were.
It is not a defence against an agent that has decided to forge, and the real
remedy remains not launching agent sessions on the host.

Tests EXECUTE the hook with a real JSON envelope rather than asserting on its
source text, which would go green whenever the prose survives an inverted
predicate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat(#1816): refuse a credentialed GitHub write from a HOST session

commits.messageBody:
Root cause: the bot-token allowance used `MINTS_BOT_TOKEN.search(command)` over
the ENTIRE command, so any command merely CONTAINING `gh-app-token.sh` was
treated as having minted the bot token and allowed. On a host session both of
these wrote under the founder's account:

    gh issue comment 1816 --body "see gh-app-token.sh"
    echo gh-app-token.sh; gh pr merge 1816

That is the exact incident class the gate exists to stop. A substring is not a
position - the same matcher-boundary shape as #2124, where a predicate was
checked against the wrong axis. Found by the security voter on #2172.

The command is now split into simple commands on `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, newline,
backtick and `$(`, and each is judged on its own. A segment invoking `gh` is
allowed only if THAT segment names an identity with a `GH_TOKEN=` assignment.

The discriminant is deliberately "an identity was named", not "the value came
from the broker": `T="$(gh-app-token.sh)"; GH_TOKEN="$T" gh ...` is the
established two-step form in this repo and the token's value is not knowable
from the text. The threat is the AMBIENT credential - on the host, `gh` with no
GH_TOKEN is the founder.

Two further review findings fixed:
- `git -C <path> push` was not matched: a bare non-flag argument between `git`
  and `push` broke the alternation.
- The deny message offered `GH_TOKEN=... gh ...` as the remedy even when denying
  `git push`. Minting GH_TOKEN does not re-route git, which authenticates
  through the credential helper or SSH, so that remedy could not work. The
  message is now per-verb and says so.
- Dropped the "measured 14-16ms over five runs" figure from the docstring: it
  was an assertion with no artifact in the diff (skeptic voter).

Two anchors needed care and are recorded so they are not "simplified" later:
`$(` opens a new command context, so it must split segments or
`x=$(gh pr view 1)` reads as one segment starting `x=` and never matches; and
the command word must be `gh(?=\s|$)` rather than `gh\b`, because a hyphen is a
word boundary and `gh\b` matches inside `gh-app-token.sh` itself.

Six regression tests added, one per reported bypass. Mutation re-verified with
the substitution ASSERTED to land first - an earlier run reported a surviving
mutant that turned out to be a no-op edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
